response:
You make a fair point, and I don't want to pretend there's no nuance here. There genuinely are things offices do well — spontaneous collaboration, easier onboarding for new people, that sense of shared momentum. I can see why some people genuinely prefer being in person.

But I don't think "it depends on the individual" fully captures it either. The evidence is pretty lopsided — the flexible arrangements tend to win on productivity and retention for most knowledge workers. So I'd say: both approaches have real merits, and the right answer does depend on the person and the role. I just also think the scales are tipped further toward autonomy than many office-mandate arguments admit. Does that feel fairer to you?
